3.6.2. The Dyads on the Tied and the Triads on the Wholesome:
Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is subject to the fetters (*ganthaniya*), a wholesome state subject to the fetters arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Dependent on a wholesome state not subject to the fetters (*aganthaniya*), a wholesome state not subject to the fetters arises by way of root-condition.

(Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are two; under object-condition there are two ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are two. (Abbreviated; similar to the progression of the mundane and supramundane.)

Dependent on a state that is both capable of being a tie (*ganthaniya*) and indeterminate (*abyākata*), and a state that is incapable of being a tie and indeterminate, there arises a state that is capable of being a tie and indeterminate by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

3.6.6. The Dyad of the Fettered and the Fetterable Dissociated from the Fetters; the Wholesome Triplet.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the ties and is subject to the ties, a wholesome state arises that is dissociated from the ties and is subject to the ties, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the ties and is not subject to the ties, a wholesome state arises that is dissociated from the ties and is not subject to the ties, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the ties and subject to the ties and a state that is dissociated from the ties and not subject to the ties, both being indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the ties and subject to the ties and indeterminate, by way of root condition.
